evaluations.label: A
errors: Surnames given as Knopf, Mengveld and Jökens do not match the transcript (Dirk Meinfeld, Xavier Juergens; the project manager gives only 'Mark').
States the UI designer's name was 'not captured', but he introduces himself as Nick Broer at 00:44.
'Rational changes only' inverts the sense of the UI designer's point, which was to avoid radical changes and stick to what is familiar.
Says the minutes and materials are stored in the shared projects folder; the project manager said they will put them there, which is a minor tense issue.
strengths: Mostly faithful to the transcript, with no major invented content.
Covers the key numbers (25 euro selling price, about 12.50 euro production cost) and that scope is a TV remote only.
Captures all four animal metaphors and the three-phase process.
Notes the 30-minute reconvene and that the personal coach will hand out assignments.
weaknesses: No action items section and no owners, so it is weak on who does what.
Does not mention that the marketing expert had nothing to share yet but had ideas.
Does not mention the whiteboard responsiveness complaint.

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'TS3012a' project code is not in the transcript, so it is unsupported.
Names are inconsistent and wrong: Markoff, Dirk Mangfelt, Savier Jokins. The UI designer is left as 'Speaker 4' even though he says his name (Nick Broer).
Says Speaker 4 'clarifies' the TV-only scope; he asked the question and the project manager answered it.
Says Savier suggests lightweight materials that are 'aesthetically impactful'; he only said the material should be light.
Lists 'what specific lightweight materials' as an open question that was never raised.
Action items are generic restatements of roles, not assignments made in the meeting, and have no owners.
strengths: Thorough structure: summary, outline, open questions and next steps.
Includes the 25 euro and 12.50 euro figures, the 30-minute reconvene, and the personal assignments.
Records the open questions on multi-remote scope and accessibility.
weaknesses: Several invented details and wrong attributions.
Misses the whiteboard responsiveness complaint and that the marketing expert had no input yet.
Action items are vague and ownerless.
Inconsistent naming makes it hard to know who is who.

evaluations.label: C
errors: The action item uses the name 'Dirk Mengveld' (transcript: Dirk Meinfeld), and other names are only first names.
'Urged familiarity and rational changes' repeats the garbled wording and loses the intended meaning of no radical changes.
Some timestamps are slightly off from where the points were actually made.
strengths: Most faithful to who said what: dolphin by the UI designer, elephant by Dirk, tiger by Xavier, ant by Mark.
Records the TV-only scope confirmation, the accessibility discussion, and the light material remark with correct attribution.
Captures the price numbers and the UI designer's remark that there is not much room to work with.
Captures that Dirk had ideas but nothing ready, with a correct follow-up action item.
Includes the whiteboard responsiveness complaint and the coach-assigned individual work.
Has timestamps and a clear summary.
weaknesses: Only one action item; it omits other follow-ups such as Mark putting the minutes in the folder, which appears only in the body.
Does not give the UI designer's name.
Some bullets are wordy for a short meeting.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Assigns 'Provide personal assignments to team members' to Mark; the transcript says the personal coach will give assignments.
Gives the UI designer an action 'Prepare intuitive design concepts', which was never assigned.
Gives Xavier an action 'Address material considerations for lightweight design'; he only remarked that the material should be light.
Dolphin described as 'smooth design'; the UI designer said freedom, and no one called the dolphin smooth.
Names are wrong (Mark Knopp, Xavier Juukens, Dirk Mankveld).
Describes a '30-minute break'; it is a reconvene after individual work.
Several timestamps are far from where the topics occur.
strengths: Has an action items section by person.
Covers the scope, price, accessibility and light-material points, and the marketing expert bringing input later.
weaknesses: Action items are partly invented or misattributed, which is risky in a notes tool.
Thin on the animal exercise and who drew what.
Thin on the meeting's context and the three-phase process detail.
Does not say who said what on scope or accessibility.

rationale: C is the most accurate and complete: correct attributions, key numbers, the TV-only scope, the accessibility and light-material points, the whiteboard complaint, and the one action that was actually stated (Dirk to share marketing ideas). A is accurate and clear but has no action items and wrongly says the UI designer's name was not captured. B has more structure but invents a project code, misattributes the scope clarification, adds an invented open question about materials, and has ownerless generic action items. D has the most problematic action items: it gives Mark the coach's job and invents assignments for the UI designer and Xavier, so a reader would act on wrong information.
